definition: Structured k-nearest neighbours (SkNN) is a machine learning algorithm that generalizes k-nearest neighbors (k-NN).
details: k-NN supports binary classification, multiclass classification, and regression, whereas SkNN allows training of a classifier for general structured output. For instance, a data sample might be a natural language sentence, and the output could be an annotated parse tree. Training a classifier consists of showing many instances of ground truth sample-output pairs. After training, the SkNN model is able to predict the corresponding output for new, unseen sample instances; that is, given a natural language sentence, the classifier can produce the most likely parse tree.

explainer.lead: A machine learning algorithm that generalizes k-nearest neighbors from discrete or real outputs to general structured outputs. It matters because many tasks, like parsing a sentence, produce structured objects rather than a single label.

tiers.eli5: Instead of picking one of a few answers for a new example, it hands back a whole arranged answer, like a diagram, built from what similar examples had.
tiers.practitioner: Trained on ground-truth sample-output pairs, it predicts outputs for unseen samples; a pitfall is that output complexity makes training and inference costly compared to plain k-NN.
tiers.paperLevel: SkNN generalizes k-NN, which supports binary classification, multiclass classification and regression, to training a classifier for general structured output; training shows many ground-truth sample-output pairs, after which it predicts outputs for new instances.

explainer.example: A natural language sentence is the sample and an annotated parse tree is the output; after training on such pairs, SkNN predicts a parse tree for a new sentence.
